title: Accessibility of the colimit closure of a small compact family
statement: Use the fixed nested universes, smallness, local smallness, infinite regular cardinals, $\kappa$-compactness and accessibility from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and coherent diagrams, full subcategories, equivalences and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\kappa$ be an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe, let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small infinity category admitting all small colimits, and let $G$ be a small set of $\kappa$-compact objects of $\mathcal E$. There is a replete full subcategory $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal E$ containing $G$ with the following properties. It is closed under all small colimits computed in $\mathcal E$ (the empty colimit is included), and it is $\kappa$-accessible. Its inclusion preserves all small colimits. More precisely, there is an essentially small full subcategory $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal H$ of objects that are $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal E$ such that every object of $\mathcal H$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit in $\mathcal E$ of objects of $\mathcal A$. The subcategory $\mathcal H$ is minimal with respect to containing $G$, being replete and being closed under small colimits. Replete means closed under equivalence in $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, proof of (6) implies (1), printed pp. 458-460, for the compact-generation construction; Corollary 5.3.4.15 for compactness of kappa-small colimits; Propositions 5.3.5.10 and 5.3.5.11(1), printed pp. 406-407, for extension into a category admitting filtered colimits and its full faithfulness; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), printed p. 404, for the restricted-Yoneda right adjoint and hence ambient colimit preservation. The hull formulation is an agent-formulated consequence, not a verbatim statement of Theorem 5.5.1.1. No ambient presentability is used. This is the general compact-generation input to Gepner–Haugseng Proposition A.5.9. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Construct an increasing family of replete full subcategories $\mathcal A_\alpha\subseteq\mathcal E$, for ordinals $\alpha\leq\kappa$. Let $\mathcal A_0$ be the replete full subcategory on $G$. At a successor, let $\mathcal A_{\alpha+1}$ consist of all objects equivalent to ambient colimits of $\kappa$-small diagrams in $\mathcal A_\alpha$. This contains $\mathcal A_\alpha$ by the one-object diagram, and includes an initial object by the empty diagram. At a nonzero limit take the full subcategory on the union of the preceding object collections. Each stage is essentially small: the base follows from [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory], and the successor from the bounded-colimit clause of [lem-coef-locally-small-infinity-size-calculus], applied with $\beta=\kappa$. At a limit choose a small family of representatives at each earlier stage; their disjoint union is small, since the ordinal of stages is at most $\kappa\in\mathcal U$, and its replete full subcategory is essentially small by the same small-full-subcategory lemma. Put $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_\kappa$. For a $\kappa$-small diagram $q:K\to\mathcal A$, choose a stage containing each vertex. There are fewer than $\kappa$ vertices, so regularity gives a common bound $\alpha<\kappa$. Fullness implies that the entire coherent diagram, including all its higher simplices, factors through $\mathcal A_\alpha$. Its ambient colimit lies in $\mathcal A_{\alpha+1}\subseteq\mathcal A$. Thus $\mathcal A$ is closed under ambient $\kappa$-small colimits. No bound of $\kappa$ on the total number of representatives is asserted.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, proof of (6) implies (1), printed p. 460: bounded colimit closure; Proposition 5.4.1.7, p. 423. The transfinite closure and its regularity bound are spelled out here.

proof.text: Every object of $\mathcal A$ is $\kappa$-compact in $\mathcal E$. Prove this simultaneously with the stage construction: it holds for $G$ by hypothesis and is invariant under equivalence because equivalent objects have equivalent corepresented mapping-space functors; at a successor apply [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] to the defining $\kappa$-small diagram, using that $\mathcal E$ has all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits; at a limit every object already lies in a preceding stage. Moreover every replete full subcategory of $\mathcal E$ containing $G$ and closed under small colimits contains every $\mathcal A_\alpha$, by the same induction, and hence contains $\mathcal A$. Choose a small quasicategory $C$ and an equivalence $q:C\simeq\mathcal A$, with coherent inverse $r$, and write $i:C\to\mathcal E$ for the composite full inclusion. Then $C$ admits $\kappa$-small colimits and $i$ preserves them. Indeed, for a diagram $p:K\to C$, its ambient colimit exists and lies in $\mathcal A$ by step 1. The mapping-space colimit test of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] shows that this ambient cocone is also colimiting in the full subcategory $\mathcal A$, because every test object of $\mathcal A$ is an object of $\mathcal E$. Conversely, a colimiting cocone in $C$ has apex in $\mathcal A$ and satisfies the same test against every object of $\mathcal A$; comparing it with the ambient colimiting cocone (whose apex is also in $\mathcal A$) gives an equivalence of apices and cocones in the full subcategory. Thus every colimiting cocone of $C$ maps to an ambient colimiting cocone. Transport along $q,r$ gives the same conclusion in $C$, and $i$ is fully faithful with $\kappa$-compact image and preserves $\kappa$-small colimits.

source.place: Corollary 5.3.4.15, printed p. 401; compactness induction in Theorem 5.5.1.1, p. 460. The minimality induction and full-subcategory mapping-space test are explicit.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], $I=\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(C)\subseteq\mathcal P(C)$ is $\kappa$-accessible and admits all small colimits, and every object of $I$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of Yoneda objects $j(c)$. Apply the extension and full-faithfulness clauses of [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] to $i:C\to\mathcal E$. The hypotheses are smallness of $C$, local smallness and existence of filtered colimits in $\mathcal E$, and full faithfulness and ambient compactness from step 2. Obtain a fully faithful functor $F:I\to\mathcal E$ preserving small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, with $Fj\simeq i$, and an equivalence from $I$ onto its replete full essential image. The last clause of the extension node, which assumes a presentable target, is not used.

Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-cocone-representatives] to the small quasicategory $C$ of step 2. Its colimiting subfamily gives a small collection $R$ representing all $\kappa$-small colimiting cocones in $C$, including the empty one. Apply the small-data clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion]. It realizes $P_R(C)$ as the full reflective subcategory of $\mathcal P(C)$ local for $s_\lambda:\operatorname{colim}_Kyp\to y(a)$, for $\lambda\in R$, with generator $j_R=Ly$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and its proof, printed pp. 412-415; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), p. 404; Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415. The local-presheaf identification is written out rather than applying Proposition 5.5.1.9 to a nonpresentable ambient category.

proof.text: For every $X\in\mathcal P(C)$, [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-colimit-locality] identifies locality for $s_\lambda$ with the comparison $X(a)\to\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}X(p(k))$ being an equivalence, with its specified cocone maps. The representatives from step 4 suffice for all $\kappa$-small colimiting cocones: pulling a cocone back along an isomorphism of shapes only relabels the comparison and its limiting cone. Since $C$ admits $\kappa$-small colimits by step 2, [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-ind-criterion] identifies this condition exactly with membership in $I=\operatorname{Ind}_\kappa(C)$. Thus $P_R(C)$ and $I$ have the same objects as replete full subcategories of $\mathcal P(C)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and its proof, printed pp. 412-415; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), p. 404; Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415. The local-presheaf identification is written out rather than applying Proposition 5.5.1.9 to a nonpresentable ambient category.

proof.text: Every representable $y(c)$ is local by the last clause of [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-colimit-locality], since each member of $R$ is colimiting in $C$. Let $J:I\hookrightarrow\mathcal P(C)$ be inclusion. For $z\in I$, adjunction and fullness give $\operatorname{Map}_I(Ly(c),z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(y(c),Jz)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_I(j(c),z)$, naturally in $c,z$. The Yoneda full-faithfulness in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied also to $I^{\mathrm{op}}$, identifies the representing functors coherently: $Ly\simeq j$. Hence the generator $j_R$ identifies with $j$ under step 5. This is just uniqueness of representing objects, not a new preservation assertion.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and its proof, printed pp. 412-415; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), p. 404; Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415. The local-presheaf identification is written out rather than applying Proposition 5.5.1.9 to a nonpresentable ambient category.

proof.text: By step 2, $i:C\to\mathcal E$ sends every member of $R$ to a colimiting cocone. The universal property of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] therefore gives $T:I\to\mathcal E$ preserving all small colimits, with $Tj\simeq i$, using the identification of categories in step 5 and of generators in step 6. Its target hypothesis is existence of all small colimits, which holds for $\mathcal E$; presentability of $\mathcal E$ is not needed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.6.2 and its proof, printed pp. 412-415; Corollary 5.3.5.4(3), p. 404; Example 5.3.6.8, p. 415. The local-presheaf identification is written out rather than applying Proposition 5.5.1.9 to a nonpresentable ambient category.

proof.text: Both $F$ and $T$ preserve small $\kappa$-filtered colimits and restrict to $i$ along $j$. Full faithfulness of the restriction equivalence in [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension] gives a coherent equivalence $F\simeq T$ compatible with these restrictions. Consequently $F$ preserves all small colimits. Let $\mathcal H$ be its replete full essential image, with equivalence $Q:I\simeq\mathcal H$ and inclusion $J:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow\mathcal E$. For any small diagram $b:K\to\mathcal H$, use a coherent inverse of $Q$ to lift it to $\widetilde b:K\to I$. Its colimit exists in $I$ by step 3. The image cocone with apex $Q(\operatorname{colim}_K\widetilde b)$ is colimiting internally by the mapping-space test and the inverse equivalence. Its ambient image is the $F$-image of that cocone, so is colimiting by the all-colimit preservation just proved. Thus $\mathcal H$ admits all small colimits, is closed under small ambient colimits, and $J$ preserves all of them, including the empty one.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.5.10, p. 406, and the full-essential-image conclusion of Proposition 5.3.5.11(1), p. 407; equivalence and colimit mapping-space tests applied explicitly.

proof.text: The subcategory $\mathcal A$ lies in $\mathcal H$ because $Fj\simeq i$ and $q$ is essentially surjective. For $h\in\mathcal H$, choose $x\in I$ with $h\simeq F(x)$. A defining small $\kappa$-filtered Yoneda presentation of $x$, from [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability], is sent by $F$ to an ambient presentation of $h$ by objects of $\mathcal A$. The category $\mathcal H$ is locally small by fullness. Its filtered colimits are ambient by step 8, and for $a\in\mathcal A$ the functor $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal H}(a,-)$ is the restriction of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,-)$. Ambient $\kappa$-compactness from step 2 therefore implies compactness in $\mathcal H$. Essential smallness of $\mathcal A$ and these presentations establish exactly the definition of $\kappa$-accessibility, as well as the stronger ambient presentation required in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 5.5.1.1, proof of (6) implies (1), p. 460; Corollary 5.3.5.4, p. 404; accessibility in Proposition 5.4.2.2.

proof.text: Finally $G\subseteq\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal H$. If $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathcal E$ is any replete full subcategory containing $G$ and closed under ambient small colimits, the induction in step 2 gives $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal B$. Each object of $\mathcal H$ has the small filtered presentation of step 9 with values in $\mathcal A$, so closure and repleteness give $\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal B$. This proves minimality. If $G$ is empty, step 1 still adjoins the initial object by the empty colimit; the argument never uses an empty filtered index.

source.place: Minimality of the two closures constructed above, checked directly from the definitions, including the empty generating family.
